study.question: Does the loss from uniform width reduction arise primarily from embedding-table rank/storage, from the dimension presented to the nonlinear scorer and towers, or from their interaction? Can an 8-dimensional table with a learned lift to 16 interaction coordinates retain the stronger source click AUC with fewer parameters and lower measured prediction cost?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: uniform E8 simultaneously reduced table width, target/history/context coordinates, the coordinate-product interaction and tower input widths. It saved about half the parameters but lost 0.00286509 click AUC. Dense-half lost 0.00117365 AUC with little parameter saving; applying dense-half at E8 instead increased AUC by 0.00041215 relative to embedding_half, an exploratory interaction of +0.00158580. These single-seed results do not locate redundant capacity. Provisional mechanism: some of the E8 loss may reflect the restricted geometry and input capacity of the nonlinear interaction rather than table rank alone. Separate raw table width R from downstream field width D through learned bias-free field projections, and test all four R,D in {8,16}. An R8,D16 lift remains rank at most eight per table; it cannot recreate an unrestricted 16-dimensional lookup. Its possible benefit is a learned interaction basis and wider nonlinear readout, not restored information. This is a diagnostic hypothesis, not demonstrated redundancy or a new-architecture claim.

nearest_work.difference: Closest executable architecture: action-aware unnormalized DIN scorer over 30 masked uniform/feedback block summaries, four towers, auxiliary scorer/item gradient blocking with context gradients retained. Preserve all these operators and hidden widths; add a shared-by-table bias-free projection to decouple stored width from interaction width. Existing g1-r0006 factorial varied uniform embedding width and hidden widths, whereas this factorial holds hidden widths fixed and separates table width from downstream input width.

Archived exact-version primary text inspected at lines 175-274: field embedding concatenation, target-dependent local activation, explicit product interactions and unnormalized pooling are inherited ideas. The local source adds block compression, four tasks and path gates. This proposal studies table/interaction width separation inside that source; no exact original DIN reproduction or novelty is claimed.

Pinned implementation inspected at lines 55-200. Retain FeatureEmbeddingDict and its lookup sharing, padding and registered nn.Embedding modules. Add learned dense field projections after embedding/compression. Alias projections when their actual embedding modules are identical. Do not modify the host FeatureMap or vocabularies. Reject unexpected field dimension overrides/encoders rather than silently changing information.

Primary benchmark section 2.3 describes Zenith's separate ID paths, EST's cross-attention/feature-specific FFNs and SSR's sparse competitive filtering. None of these architectures is implemented here. The change is uniform table-to-interaction projection under an unchanged compressed source. Benchmark descriptions are not original-method full-paper audits.

inherited_components: Frozen data identity, official_offline visibility, four labels, supplied context/item/action fields, 100-event masks and temporal split.
g2-r0004-context_only source and its exact 10 blocks x 3 masked mean summaries, count weighting and uniform-click/feedback-auxiliary routing.
Action-aware unnormalized shared local activation with Dice and hidden widths 64/32; four separate towers with hidden widths 128/64.
Auxiliary functional scorer with detached parameters and cloned Dice buffers; item/action path detached for auxiliaries; context path trainable; single scorer call during inference.
Default sum of four unweighted BCEs; frozen single-pass host recipe, seed, optimizers, batch size, precision and scorers. No training-loss hook.
Framework embedding lookup and shared target/history tables, with all source fields retained.
study.proposed_difference: Four standalone cells independently set raw table width R and downstream per-field width D to 8 or 16. Every cell, including both square controls, adds one trainable bias-free R-to-D field map per unique underlying embedding module. Projections are initialized with orthogonal weights and gain sqrt(max(1,D/R)), after the source reset; this preserves average output-coordinate variance only for isotropic independent inputs. Raw histories are compressed before projection; linearity makes this equivalent in exact arithmetic to projecting each history before masked averaging. Current target and context use the same per-field maps; target/history aliases remain tied. Hidden scorer/tower widths and source gradient gates are unchanged. R8,D16 is the primary candidate; R16,D8 is a diagnostic replacement candidate, not expected to halve storage. R8,D8 and R16,D16 control for the added projection operator. Each module supplies a literal CONFIG and Model with the frozen prediction API. No new forward inputs, field removal, loss weights, data passes or optimizer changes.
predictions: Primary diagnostic: if nonlinear interaction width matters beyond table rank, AUC(table8_interact16) exceeds AUC(table8_interact8), with a smaller gap between table8_interact16 and table16_interact16 than between the two square cells. Compare the difference of D effects across R to measure interaction, without presuming its sign.

If raw table rank is the dominant limitation, table8_interact16 remains below table16_interact16 despite identical downstream input and hidden widths. If compact downstream geometry is sufficient, table16_interact8 retains AUC relative to table16_interact16, isolating a possible latency reduction without a large storage benefit.

Operational screening retention is click AUC at least 0.660146940486458 (source 0.660646940486458 minus a predeclared 0.0005 margin), total parameters at least 40% below 32060453, and both model-only p50/p95 latency at least 5% below source replay 11.77057/11.90825 ms. Report whole-validation throughput separately; prefer a concurrent host timing control if authorized. These screening thresholds are not a confidence interval or established noninferiority. A joint efficiency claim needs repeated quality and timing support.

Embedding parameters should equal 15896608 at R8 or 31793216 at R16 if the original sharing/schema audit passes. With K unique projection owners, total counts should be 16048645+64K (R8,D8), 16163845+128K (R8,D16), 31945253+128K (R16,D8), and 32060453+256K (R16,D16). K and actual counts must be measured by the host. These are storage arithmetic predictions, not latency predictions.

Report all four AUC/logloss pairs, auxiliary mean separately, train/allocated-GPU/wall seconds, examples processed, peak memory, parameter split, validation inference seconds, throughput and p50/p95 batch latency. Source cart/fav/buy AUCs already trail baseline-din substantially; retaining click AUC must never be reported as retaining all-task quality. Use only existing history-length slice rules and show positives/negatives; slices and cross-cell effects remain exploratory until repeated.
falsifiers: No advantage of R8,D16 over R8,D8, together with a persistent gap to R16,D16, rejects the tested interaction-width rescue; it does not refute every mixed-width or low-rank design.
Neither R8 cell reaches the predeclared source-retention margin, or retention fails in later paired repetitions: no supported claim of preserving the stronger source at half table storage.
A compact-table cell that retains AUC but does not improve measured latency/throughput fails the joint prediction-cost claim. Parameter savings or FLOP estimates alone are insufficient.

If R16,D16 materially shifts quality relative to g1-r0006-source_replay, the new projection/optimization is consequential. Attribution against the unchanged source must include that shift; benefit cannot be ascribed to width allocation alone.

Failure of projection/compression equivalence, empty-history or padding invariance, parameter alias/optimizer audits, finite backward, or source gradient-gate tests invalidates the implementation and blocks substantive host training. Log the failed attempt and its cost; do not alter frozen inputs or contracts.
alternative_explanations: One training seed, changed initialization shapes and trainable projections can change optimization speed under the one-pass recipe; learned table rank and convergence are not separable from these observations alone. Same-seed source replay exactly reproduces AUC and is not an independent repetition.

Square projections are trainable rotations/scalings, not forward-identical controls for the original source. Their comparison to existing unprojected endpoints measures combined projection/optimization effects. No evidence here identifies redundancy of particular fields or frequency groups.

At fixed D, projection parameter counts differ by K*D*(16-8), even though nonlinear scorer/tower input sizes and hidden widths match. At fixed R, projection shape, dense input parameters, projection arithmetic and activation memory all vary with D. These are part of the allocated-capacity intervention, not a strict parameter-matched architecture contest.

R16,D8 still has an effective rank-eight linear map and cannot independently exploit all sixteen raw coordinates downstream; it is an overparameterized factorization control, not proof of higher effective representation rank. R8,D16 likewise has at most rank eight despite sixteen output coordinates.

Bias-free projection commutes with masked averaging in exact arithmetic; BF16 accumulation/casting can create small numeric differences. Host equivalence checks must distinguish tolerance-sized differences from operator errors.

Many small field projections, non-contiguous splits and concatenations can erase savings. Source inference wall time varied 24.46 to 26.72 seconds on an identical replay although model p50 was stable; loading time and accelerator noise can explain throughput changes.

Aliased embedding modules preserve shared projections, but cross-source sharing can let auxiliary context gradients reach a shared item table/projection. Keep source computational path gates and audit ownership; no exclusive semantic ownership claim follows from a detach.

All evidence is validation-only on the frozen released offline history policy, including potentially immature delayed feedback. No deployment-valid point-in-time claim, original-method reproduction claim, or verified priority claim.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Earlier uniform reductions failed to preserve click AUC, justifying further allocation diagnostics. Available observations do not identify per-ID or per-field redundancy or frequency support, so do not expand IDs or adopt Zenith tokens. The primary-paper record is link-only; audited benchmark section is limited evidence.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None adopted from Zenith. All fields receive the same table width and projection-width policy.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Uniform storage-to-interaction maps under the compressed DIN source, rather than separate ID expansion and token interaction paths. No priority claim.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If uniform factorization remains inadequate, selective capacity could be reconsidered only with authorized diagnostics and matched-storage controls.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Feature-specific FFNs and repeated sequence cross-attention would change the source mechanism and cost beyond this table/interaction attribution. Rejection is study-specific; no negative EST transfer has been measured.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None: the bias-free maps only change embedding coordinates; no cross-attention or feature-specific nonlinear FFNs are added.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Retain one action-aware compressed DIN readout; benchmark EST uses cross-attention and feature-specific FFNs. Original EST paper remains unaudited.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Failure of all tested storage/interaction configurations would motivate a separately controlled interaction replacement, without establishing that EST would work.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Retrieved competitive sparse filtering does not directly separate table storage from interaction coordinates and may not produce actual speedups. No observed activation redundancy supports selecting this operator now.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None: no competitive filtering, learned sparsity or multi-view fusion.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Dense linear projection before the inherited scorer differs from benchmark SSR's sparse filtering after target pooling. Original SSR paper is not audited and no general novelty claim follows.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A later measured redundancy diagnosis could justify sparse-versus-dense controls at matched capacity and cost; current results do not test SSR.
